assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one DNA base to another (deaminase fused to a Cas nickase or dead Cas9) without double-strand breaks. This is a genuine molecular-design invention that changed how genome stability and point-mutation disease are approached. Cytosine and adenine base editors are in wide laboratory use and in clinical trials, which makes the impact concrete and not only prospective. From my vantage in DNA integrity and mutagenesis, avoiding double-strand-break repair is a conceptual advance in its own right.
assessment.attribution: David R. Liu led the invention, and Komor and Gaudelli were the lead trainees on the cytosine and adenine editors. The prize allows at most three names, and the field's foundational CRISPR credit was already awarded in 2020. I propose Liu alone as the cleanest configuration. Whether a trainee should share the prize is an open question. Nishida and Kondo's earlier deaminase-targeting work is a possible priority complication.
assessment.maturity: Cytosine editors date to 2016 and adenine editors to 2017, so there are nearly ten years of independent validation. Clinical-stage base-editing therapies are reported (I have not verified the specifics), and recognition looks timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views base editing as chemistry or as biology and medicine given the 2020 CRISPR prize.
Overlap with prime editing (B018), which may be better treated as a later extension.
Priority claims from Nishida and Kondo and whether trainees should share credit.
Off-target deamination (DNA and RNA) and bystander editing remain active concerns.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by heterobifunctional PROTACs and molecular glue degraders such as thalidomide analogs redirects E3 ubiquitin ligases to chosen proteins. It created a new pharmacological modality built on chemical design. It also supplied a mechanism (cereblon) for a historically notorious drug, and it is a clear molecular-chemistry story with growing clinical translation.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies established the PROTAC concept; Sakamoto was the co-inventor of the first PROTAC. Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target. Ciulli and Gray carried the field forward but later. A three-way split between PROTAC concept and the molecular glue mechanism is plausible, but the credit between Crews, Deshaies and Sakamoto is not fully settled in my view. Ciulli is a strong alternative.
assessment.maturity: The first PROTAC appeared in 2001. Many compounds are now in clinical trials, and the degrader field is broadly independently confirmed. Approval of a PROTAC drug would strengthen the case, and I am uncertain whether that has happened.
uncertainties: Allocation among Crews, Deshaies, Sakamoto, Handa, Ciulli and Gray is contested.
Clinical outcomes for degraders are still emerging.
PROTAC and molecular-glue mechanisms may need different recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing (Solexa/Illumina sequencing-by-synthesis, and pyrosequencing-based 454) made genomes cheap and routine. It underlies genome-stability, mutation, cancer and nucleotide-metabolism research like my own. The chemistry of reversible terminators and clonal amplification is foundational and has had enormous lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman invented the Solexa chemistry, and Rothberg led the first commercial massively parallel platform (454). Mayer and Ju contributed related ideas, and I am uncertain how their contributions rank relative to the core three. Sanger and Gilbert were recognized in 1980, and the 2020 chemistry prize was for CRISPR, so there is no direct prior-prize conflict that I know of.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature: the technology has been in use since the mid-2000s and is broadly confirmed. It is arguably overdue, and the open question is allocation.
uncertainties: Contested attribution: Mayer, Ju and others also have claims, and platform commercialization raises corporate-credit questions.
Whether the committee treats this as chemistry or as a biology and medicine tool.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles made practical delivery of siRNA and mRNA possible and underpin the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines and siRNA drugs. The physical-chemical principle of pH-dependent ionizable lipids and rapid-mixing assembly is original and is documented by clinical use. The 2023 Medicine prize recognized nucleoside modification, not delivery, so the delivery chemistry remains unrecognized.
assessment.attribution: Cullis led the foundational LNP and ionizable-lipid work, Anderson and Langer developed lipidoid libraries, and MacLachlan, Hope and Madden were key coauthors. Choosing three from six is difficult, and the allocation of credit is a real unresolved issue.
assessment.maturity: Mature: licensed siRNA drug Onpattro and mRNA vaccines have been given to billions. Recognition appears timely.
uncertainties: Credit is spread across many people, and patent and commercial disputes complicate a clean attribution.
Possible overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize in the public perception of the mRNA story.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reversible m6A modification of RNA, with writers, erasers and readers, established a dynamic epitranscriptome. Chuan He's FTO demethylase and reader-protein work gave a chemical-biology framework, and the mapping of m6A by Dominissini, Rechavi and Jaffrey allowed transcriptome-wide study. It is relevant to nucleotide and nucleic-acid chemistry and to disease.
assessment.attribution: He is the strongest candidate for the conceptual and enzymatic discovery (FTO as a demethylase with Jia). Jaffrey and Rechavi shared the first transcriptome-wide maps in 2012. Jia, Meyer, Yang and Dominissini also contributed. Priority between He and Jaffrey and Rechavi is mixed, and I am uncertain how the committee would weigh mapping against mechanism.
assessment.maturity: About 15 years of growing confirmation, with some controversy over the quantitative resolution of mapping methods and the physiological role of FTO. Therapeutic follow-up (METTL3 inhibitors) is still early.
uncertainties: Disputed attribution between mapping and enzymology.
Technical controversies over m6A detection and stoichiometry.
The field may be seen as better fitted to biology and medicine.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Shokat's design of covalent inhibitors for the G12C mutant of KRAS opened a target class considered undruggable and, together with analog-sensitive kinase chemical genetics, is a clear case of chemical design solving a biological problem. It has led to approved drugs (sotorasib and adagrasib), which I believe but have not verified in detail.
assessment.attribution: Shokat is the single credited name and the decisive contributor to the covalent G12C strategy. The drug-development work involved company teams (Araxes, Amgen, Mirati) not listed here, so the configuration is simple but potentially incomplete.
assessment.maturity: The foundational paper dates to 2013, and clinical validation followed. It is fairly mature, though long-term resistance and durability data continue to emerge.
uncertainties: Industrial contributors are not in the credited names.
Medicinal-chemistry prizes are less usual for the Chemistry committee, and a single-person prize may feel narrow.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Activity-based protein profiling uses covalent probes to read the functional state of enzymes in complex proteomes. It connects chemistry to metabolism and enzymology and has produced drug-discovery platforms and many targets. The concept is original and broadly used.
assessment.attribution: Cravatt developed and generalized the approach and Bogyo made important protease-probe contributions. Overkleeft and Weerapana are also credited, and Cravatt is clearly central. Whether one name or two is correct is open.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with about 25 years of independent adoption and chemoproteomic extensions into covalent ligand discovery.
uncertainties: Attribution beyond Cravatt, and priority relative to earlier affinity-labeling work.
Breadth of method rather than a single discovery may weigh against it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation of biomolecules organizes cells into membraneless compartments. The 2009 P-granule work showed liquid-like behavior and shifted a basic view of cellular organization. It links to nucleolar and DNA-repair condensates relevant to my field.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman made the foundational demonstration, and Rosen, Pappu and Mittag provided the physical-chemical framework. Two names are the most defensible, though the credit split is disputed.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly growing but still contested: in vivo physiological relevance, the definition of phase separation versus other assemblies, and many reports of condensates in disease are debated. The field may be premature for a prize.
uncertainties: The physiological relevance of many reported condensates remains debated.
Credit is distributed across theory and experiment.
The field may be seen as cell biology rather than chemistry.
